battle.name: 猶太戰爭
battle.brief: 公元66年猶大起兵反抗羅馬統治，維斯帕先平定加利利與猶太南部，提多則於公元70年攻陷耶路撒冷、焚毀第二聖殿。卡面的羅馬方陣盾貫穿全役：野戰靠盾緣互咬成連續防線，圍城時拼成龜甲陣護住撞槌與攻城塔推進。

kit.name: 羅馬方陣盾
kit.history: 凸面的長方盾。羅馬的防線靠盾緣咬住盾緣，不是靠盾牌多厚。

countries: 這場戰爭是公元66年至73、74年間，羅馬帝國在猶大行省對猶太反抗勢力進行的長期鎮壓戰。羅馬一方以皇帝尼祿為最高統帥，敘利亞總督蓋斯圖斯·加利烏斯在66年秋先鋒出手，翌年由自羅馬返回的維斯帕先以「猶太戰爭總指揮」的頭銜接手，公元70年再由其子提多接管耶路撒冷戰線；作戰序列包括第十弗拉提尼斯、第十五阿波里納里斯、第六鐵甲、第五馬其頓與第十二閃電等軍團，以及各類輔助軍與騎兵隊。羅馬陣營還有兩位附庸王朝的配合：希律王朝末代國王阿格利帕二世以加利利與佩列亞為基地站在羅馬一邊，其父阿格利帕一世早年在聖殿問題上替猶太人擋過一次皇帝的索取。猶太一方並非統一軍隊：耶路撒冷由大祭司安努斯與其子以利亞撒·班·阿南尼亞掌握的熱誠派主導，另有西蒙·巴·基奧拉等民粹領袖與聖殿守軍首領以利亞撒·西蒙；加利利由約瑟夫斯率領，武裝實力最完整；提比亞的猶斯都與約翰·基斯卡拉各領武裝；撒瑪利亞人與阿拉伯方面的騎兵站在羅馬一邊，另有奴隸與外邦人被編入猶太軍。此戰最深的裂痕在猶太內部，王族之家與大祭司之家、耶路撒冷派與加利利派、穩健派與熱誠派屢次互相掣肘，決定了守軍在城破前的崩潰速度。
countriesEn: This war was a long campaign in which the Roman Empire crushed the Jewish revolt in the province of Judaea between AD 66 and 73/74. On the Roman side the supreme commander was the emperor Nero, who in 66 sent the governor Cestius Gallus of Syria to open the fighting; in 67 the overall command passed to Vespasian, who returned from the capital to take up the post of commander of the Jewish war, and in 70 his son Titus took over the siege of Jerusalem. The order of battle included the Legio X Fretensis, the Legio XV Apollinaris, the Legio VI Ferrata, the Legio V Macedonica and the Legio XII Fulminata, together with auxiliary infantry and cavalry detachments. Two client dynasties stood with Rome: Herod Agrippa II, the last king of the Herodian line, ruled Galilee and Peraea on Rome's behalf, while his father Agrippa I had earlier shielded the Temple from one of the emperor's demands. The Jewish side was never a single army. In Jerusalem the Zealots around the high priest Ananus and his son Eleazar ben Ananias took the lead, with populist leaders such as Simon bar Giora and the Temple commander Eleazar ben Simon; Galilee was commanded by Josephus and fielded the most complete force; Justus of Tiberias and John of Gischala led separate armed bands; Samaritans and Arab contingents fought on the Roman side, and slaves and non-Jews were enrolled into the Jewish forces. The deepest fault lines ran inside the revolt itself: the royal house against the house of the high priest, the Jerusalem party against the Galileans, the moderates against the Zealots. Those divisions decided how fast the defenders collapsed once the walls were breached.
people: 羅馬方面的關鍵人物分三層。皇帝尼祿在66年召回巡撫龐提烏斯·皮拉，改派行政長官與財政官約瑟夫接管稅務，並令敘利亞總督蓋斯圖斯·加利烏斯進兵，該軍在耶路撒冷敗退後，戰區被整併交給維斯帕先；維斯帕先於67年抵任，圍攻約塔帕塔、平定加利利與猶太南部，69年在內戰中成為皇帝，其子提多隨軍並在70年接任指揮，終於攻下耶路撒冷。工程與突擊環節的關鍵人物是羅馬工程師尼哥拉，他率精銳中隊在70年破開城北第三道城牆；阿格利帕二世既是羅馬的附庸，也是提多的顧問，其妹貝勒尼基在羅馬向提多陳情，成為全城陷落前最出名的一次求情，尼祿的皇後波帕亞則是阿格利帕二世在宮廷上的靠山。猶太方面的關鍵人物同樣密集：大祭司安努斯、其子以利亞撒·班·阿南尼亞（在聖殿議事堂上拒絕向羅馬進貢並率先號召抵抗）、西蒙·巴·基奧拉（後來掌握耶路撒冷城防）、其子以利亞撒·西蒙（聖殿守軍領袖）、加利利將領約瑟夫斯（兵敗後為羅馬撰寫戰史，成為今日了解此役的主要文本來源）、提比亞的猶斯都、游擊隊首領約翰·基斯卡拉，以及瑪薩達最後的守將以利亞撒·班·雅伊爾。
peopleEn: The decisive figures on the Roman side fall into three layers. The emperor Nero recalled the governor Pontius Pilate in 66, handed the tax arrangements to a new prefect and the finance official Josephus, and ordered the governor of Syria Cestius Gallus to advance; after that army was repulsed in the approaches to Jerusalem the whole theatre was consolidated and handed to Vespasian. Vespasian arrived in 67, besieged Jotapata, reduced Galilee and the Judean south, and in 69 became emperor in the civil war; his son Titus served with him, took over the command in 70 and finally took Jerusalem. The key man in the engineering and assault phases was the Roman officer Nicolaus, who led the picked cohorts that broke the Third Wall on the northern side of the city in 70. Agrippa II was both Rome's client and Titus's adviser, and his sister Berenice made the most famous appeal of the whole war in Rome, pleading before Titus; the empress Poppaea was Agrippa II's protector at court. The Jewish side is equally crowded with named figures: the high priest Ananus, his son Eleazar ben Ananias, who refused the tribute to Rome in the Temple assembly and first called for resistance, Simon bar Giora, who later took charge of the city's defences, his son Eleazar Simon, commander of the Temple guard, the Galilean commander Josephus, who after his defeat wrote the war history for the Romans and is the principal source for the campaign today, Justus of Tiberias, the guerrilla leader John of Gischala, and finally Eleazar ben Ya'ir, the last commander at Masada.
kits: 卡面的羅馬方陣盾是此役羅馬軍的基本裝備，貫穿全戰線。帝國遠征兵每名列兵都攜帶一面凸面長方盾，約高一百零五至一百二十公分、寬約六十公分，木胎蒙皮、中央有金屬盾紐、四邊包鐵，估計重量在六至八公斤之間，表面彩繪各軍團徽記，第十軍團用的是公牛。它在體系裡的功能正如卡面所述：羅馬的防線靠盾緣互相咬合成一條連續的帶，靠的是接面平整與列隊密度，而不是盾體的厚度。作戰上，進攻前先以標槍齊射削弱敵陣，列陣後以盾相接步步推進；接近城牆時，士兵把盾舉在頭頂與身前拼成龜甲陣，在弩砲火力下護住撞槌與攻城塔的基部；圍城時則改用壁面盾保護工兵與填壕作業。除此之外，羅軍裝備線上還有短劍與雙刃匕首、輔助步兵的長矛與輕標槍、輔助騎兵每隊約三百二十人配大盾長矛，攻城用的配重式投石機與大型弩砲、可拆卸的鐵頭撞槌與可逐段推行的攻城塔，依維特魯維烏斯記載塔高約十五至二十公尺，以及供圍城軍取水的木製鏈式水車。猶太方面的武器庫則雜亂得多：城頭以石塊、弓箭與標槍招呼羅軍，另有從城內推出的投射機與農具改造成的長矛，馬薩達的守軍還備有大量石制投射物。最關鍵的一點是，猶太軍沒有可互相咬合的制式盾牌，也沒有統一的操典，這正是城牆一破即潰的技術原因。
kitsEn: The Roman scutum on the card is the basic piece of equipment of the Roman army in this war and runs through the whole campaign. Every soldier in an imperial field army carried a convex rectangular shield roughly 105 to 120 centimetres high and about 60 centimetres wide, with a wooden core covered in hide, a metal boss at the centre, ironed edges, an estimated weight of six to eight kilograms, and the emblem of his legion painted on the face, the bull for the Tenth Legion. Its place in the system is exactly as the card states: the Roman line held because shield rims locked edge to edge into one continuous band, and that band depended on flat fitting surfaces and tight order, not on the thickness of the boards. In action, a volley of javelins opened the fight, the line advanced with shields joined, and when men neared a wall they raised the shield over head and body to build a testudo, covering the battering ram and the base of the siege tower under fire from their own artillery. During a blockade the wall-shield protected engineers and the men filling the ditch. The rest of the Roman equipment train included the short sword and the double-edged dagger, long spears and light javelins for the auxiliary infantry, auxiliary cavalry of about 320 men a troop with large shields and long lances, counterweight stone-throwers and large ballistae for the siege, a detachable iron-headed ram, a siege tower pushed forward in sections, which Vitruvius puts at some fifteen to twenty metres high, and wooden chain pumps that raised water for the besieging army. The Jewish equipment was far more miscellaneous: stones, arrows and javelins from the walls, engines pushed up from inside the city, spears made out of farm tools, and at Masada a great supply of stone missiles. The decisive point is that the Jewish army had no interlocking pattern shields and no common drill, which is the technical reason the defence collapsed as soon as the wall was breached.
tactics: 羅馬此役的戰術是一套可重複的攻城程序。野戰上，靠列兵以盾相接形成的密集正面把對手釘在原地，再用兩翼騎兵與散兵繞側；攻城上，先以包圍牆與壕溝切斷城內補給，再以弩砲與投石機壓制城頭，之後才是填壕、築壘、推攻城塔與撞槌貼牆，最後以龜甲陣護住突擊隊登城。約塔帕塔之圍最能說明這套程序：羅馬人把壕溝填平、築起攻城土壘，猶太人則在城內築起一道反向土坡抵禦，羅軍改用鐵頭撞槌破門，圍城四十餘日後守軍首領約瑟夫斯出降。耶路撒冷之圍是同一程序的放大版：第一輪進攻因守軍從城頭挖穿地道反制而失利，羅軍退回去建包圍線、造攻城塔與撞槌，第二輪以配重投石機把城頭打崩，再破第三道城牆，攻入安東尼亞兵營，最後攻入聖殿。馬薩達則是反過來的一課：南岸峭壁擋死填方，羅馬人改從北岸緩坡築起長斜坡，把攻城塔與撞槌一路推上高原，破了斜坡頂端的城牆缺口。守方這邊靠游擊、襲擊糧道與拖延，且缺乏統一指揮。
tacticsEn: The Roman tactics of this war were a repeatable siege procedure. In the field, a dense front held together by joined shields pinned the enemy in place while cavalry and skirmishers worked round the flanks. Before a city, the sequence was to cut the defenders' supplies with a circumvallation and its ditch, to neutralise the walls with ballistae and stone-throwers, and only then to fill the ditch, raise a mound, push up the siege towers and rams, and finally cover the storming parties with a testudo. The siege of Jotapata shows the sequence in miniature: the Romans filled the ditch and raised a mound against the wall, the Jews built a counter-ramp inside the town to check it, and the Romans answered with an iron-headed ram; after something over forty days the commander Josephus capitulated. The siege of Jerusalem was the same procedure enlarged. The first assault failed because the defenders tunnelled under the works and collapsed them from above; the Romans withdrew, built the circumvallation, and constructed towers and rams; the second assault brought down the parapets with counterweight throwers, opened the Third Wall, carried the Antonia fortress, and finally entered the Temple. Masada taught the opposite lesson: the cliffs on the south side defeated any attempt to fill the ground, so the Romans built a long ramp on the gentler northern shore, pushed towers and rams up the slope, and forced the breach where the ramp met the wall on the plateau. On the defending side the methods were ambush, attacks on supply lines and delay, without a unified command to hold them together.
data: 可核對的數字大致如下。戰爭始於公元66年，圍耶路撒冷有兩輪：第一輪自70年春到夏，第二輪在70年秋，聖殿在猶太曆塔穆茲月（公歷六七月間）淪陷，禁食日塔穆茲月十七日前後焚毀。提多在城北集結的羅軍，一般估計在八萬至十萬之間；約瑟夫斯記載的守軍人數從數萬到十餘萬不等，現代史家多視為誇大，他另稱攻城階段陣亡者逾一萬、被俘約四萬，戰後被押往羅馬者逾十萬。維斯帕先67年進入加利利時，本部約二萬步兵與三千二百騎兵，另有安東尼烏斯所部與各輔助軍。馬薩達圍城歷時約二至三年，自公元72或73年起，羅軍兵力約八千至九千人，守軍九百六十七人，最後僅十五人拒降。耶路撒冷城牆周長約十一至十二公里，羅馬人在馬薩達修築的包圍牆考古實測約一公里，攻城斜坡長近百公尺，羅軍營地的水車殘件至今可見。戰後耶路撒冷人口銳減，二世紀時只餘萬人量級。
dataEn: The figures that can be checked run roughly as follows. The war began in AD 66. Jerusalem was besieged twice: a first round from the spring to the summer of 70, and a second in the autumn of that year; the Temple fell in the Jewish month of Tammuz, which falls in June and July, and was burned around the fast day on the seventeenth of Tammuz. The Roman force Titus concentrated north of the city is generally estimated at between eighty thousand and a hundred thousand men. Josephus gives wildly different figures for the garrison, from tens of thousands to more than a hundred thousand, which modern historians generally treat as inflated; he adds that more than ten thousand defenders were killed in the assault, about forty thousand were taken prisoner, and that upwards of a hundred thousand Jews were carried off to Rome. When Vespasian entered Galilee in 67 he had about twenty thousand foot and three thousand two hundred horse, with the force of Antonius and the auxiliaries alongside. The blockade of Masada lasted some two to three years from 72 or 73, the Roman force numbered roughly eight to nine thousand men, the defenders numbered nine hundred and sixty-seven, and only fifteen refused to surrender. The circuit of Jerusalem's walls ran to about eleven or twelve kilometres, the Roman circumvallation at Masada measures about a kilometre, the assault ramp runs for close to a hundred metres, and the remains of the Roman water wheels are still visible in the camp. After the war the population of Jerusalem fell away sharply, leaving only a few thousand in the second century.
cause: 導火線是一連串小事攏在一起。猶大自公元6年起淪為羅馬的稅收對象，稅吏與巡撫的錢直接從聖殿庫房、葡萄園與橄欖園出；希律王朝在位時尚有緩衝，公元44年阿格利帕一世死後，王國被羅馬收為行省，阿格利帕二世只是分治加利利與佩列亞的附庸君主，本地菁英與羅馬的稅務體系長期對立。宗教上的紅線有兩條：卡里古拉曾想在聖殿立像，由阿格利帕一世擋下；尼祿允許貴族的銀像進入聖殿，又取消安尼亞斯與波的職位，改由抽籤的行政長官管理。一旦有皇帝像進入耶路撒冷，炸開的就不只是尊嚴，還有凱撒崇拜與獨一神崇拜的正面衝突。直接點火的是66年那次以核查稅戶為名的大普查，清點貨物、丈量田產、翻舊帳，基列的猶太人最先動手，接著蔓延到耶路撒冷。最後一根火柴是秋季蓋斯圖斯·加利烏斯入城取走數十塔蘭特白銀，猶太代表團要求歸還被拒，他反過來包圍聖殿城，卻在撤退時遭追擊而大敗，於是「不再有人肯聽從」成為公開的訊號。
causeEn: The trigger was a chain of small things. From AD 6 Judaea was a Roman revenue district, and the money of the tax collectors and prefects came straight out of the Temple treasury, the vineyards and the olive groves. The Herodian dynasty had provided some buffer, but after Agrippa I died in AD 44 the kingdom was taken over as a Roman province, and Agrippa II was only a client king ruling Galilee and Peraea in part, so the local elite and the Roman fiscal system stood in permanent tension. Two religious red lines ran through the period: Caligula once tried to set up an image in the Temple and was deflected by Agrippa I, and Nero allowed a silver image of the emperor to be brought into the Temple, then abolished the offices of Ananus and Boethus and put a prefect chosen by lot in charge. Once an imperial image could stand in Jerusalem, what exploded was not only a matter of honour but a head-on collision between imperial cult and the exclusive worship of one God. The thing that actually lit the fuse in 66 was the great census taken in the name of checking the tax rolls, with goods counted, land measured and old debts re-opened. The Galileans moved first and the disturbance spread to Jerusalem. The last match was the autumn entry of Cestius Gallus into the city, who took several tens of talents of silver from the treasury; when the Jewish delegation asked for it back and was refused, he surrounded the Temple quarter instead, and was then beaten back during his retreat, so that the open message became: no one will obey any more.
impact: 這場戰爭的後果延續了幾個世紀。第一，聖殿被毀、獻祭中止，耶路撒冷失去宗教首都的地位，祭司階層與整套聖殿禮儀一併崩解，城市的居民被逐批送往羅馬與帝國各地。第二，沒有聖殿的猶太教被迫以口傳《妥拉》與家庭祭禮為中心，拉比阿基瓦那一代學者在戰亂中成熟，稍後由拉比猶哈於公元二世紀編成的《密西拿》成為新的正典基礎，拉比猶太教取代了祭司國家的架構，此後兩千年它就靠這套文本在沒有國家與軍隊的情況下維持住共同體。第三，羅馬以殖民地形式接管耶路撒冷，第十軍團進駐聖殿原址，該軍的公牛徽記後來出現在耶路撒冷的市徽上，而猶太人進入城內受到限制。第四，在軍力上，羅馬從此在帝國東境長期設防，埃及、敘利亞與猶大之間形成常備的軍力配置，公元132年爆發的巴爾·科赫巴起義則是這套體制的後續壓力測試。第五，在思想上，拉比猶太教、基督教與尚未分家的猶太基督教群體在公元70年前後同時成形，而約瑟夫斯這部用希臘文寫給皇帝看的《猶太戰史》，從此成為西方記得猶太戰爭的主要文本。
impactEn: The consequences of this war ran for centuries. First, the Temple was destroyed and the sacrificial system came to an end; Jerusalem lost its standing as religious capital, the priestly hierarchy and the whole liturgy of the Temple collapsed at once, and the population was deported in batches to Rome and to the provinces. Second, a Judaism without a Temple was forced to centre itself on the oral Torah and on domestic worship; the generation of scholars around Rabbi Akiva matured in the fighting, and the Mishnah, compiled by Rabbi Judah in the second century, became the new scriptural foundation, with rabbinic Judaism taking over the institutional role of the priestly state and holding the community together for two thousand years without a state or an army. Third, Rome took Jerusalem over as a colony and the Tenth Legion was stationed on the site of the Temple; the bull badge of that legion later appears on the city's emblem, and Jews were restricted in entering the city. Fourth, in military terms Rome now kept permanent defences in the eastern provinces, with a standing force distributed between Egypt, Syria and Judaea, and the Bar Kokhba revolt of AD 132 became the next stress test of that system. Fifth, in intellectual terms rabbinic Judaism, Christianity and the still-unseparated Jewish-Christian groups all took shape around AD 70, while Josephus's history of the war, written in Greek for the emperor, became the principal text through which the West remembers the Jewish war.
result: 打完之後，羅馬在猶大取得決定性勝利但代價高昂：耶路撒冷在公元70年被提多攻陷，第二聖殿焚毀，安東尼亞兵營與大半城牆盡毀；猶太方面的武裝政黨網絡被清剿，西蒙·巴·基奧拉、其子以利亞撒等頭目相繼被羅馬處決或自殺，加利利與佩列亞最後只餘阿格利帕二世的小王國殘餘。馬薩達的據點在公元73或74年陷落，最後的守軍以自己的手了斷性命，羅軍則佔據高原，把馬薩達變成羅馬的前哨與觀察哨。戰俘被運往羅馬，提多於71年舉行凱旋式，聖殿的器皿成為廣場上的展示品，約瑟夫斯留在羅馬撰寫戰史，後來奉提多出使尼祿，並獲得賜姓弗拉維烏斯。長期看，羅馬完成了對猶太地區的直接統治，卻同時把自己放到了猶太反對羅馬這一政治結構的中心，兩百多年後公元132年的戰爭會用同一條防線再打一遍。
resultEn: When the fighting was over, Rome had won decisively in Judaea at heavy cost. Jerusalem fell to Titus in AD 70, the Second Temple was burned, the Antonia fortress and most of the walls were destroyed. The network of armed factions in Judaea was hunted down: Simon bar Giora and his son Eleazar were executed by the Romans or died by their own hand, and in Galilee and Peraea nothing survived of the old order except the small client kingdom of Agrippa II. The stronghold of Masada fell in AD 73 or 74, the last defenders killing themselves rather than surrender, and the Romans occupied the plateau, turning Masada into a Roman outpost and observation post. Captives were shipped to Rome, where Titus celebrated his triumph in AD 71 with the vessels of the Temple displayed in the forum, while Josephus stayed in Rome to write the history and was later sent by Titus to Nero, receiving the name Flavius. In the long run Rome completed its direct rule over Judaea, but in doing so it placed itself at the centre of the political structure of Jewry's resistance to Rome, and a war fought along the same defensive line would be fought all over again more than two centuries later, in AD 132.
